Destination guide

Uganda is one of Africa’s best-value wildlife countries, blending gorilla trekking, chimpanzee tracking, Nile landscapes, and savannah safari parks into one route. Its standout combination is unusually concentrated: mountain gorillas and Albertine Rift endemics in the southwest, chimpanzee forests, Nile-based wildlife at Murchison, and savannah circuits linked by road or domestic flight.

Photos: Thomas Fuhrmann (CC BY-SA 4.0) · Diego Delso (CC BY-SA 4.0). Displayed images may be resized or cropped. Photo details.

Getting around

Access is strongest through Entebbe with onward road circuits and selective domestic flights into southwestern or northern safari sectors.

Best time

Dryer months are usually easiest for gorilla trekking trails and game viewing, though Uganda remains rewarding year-round thanks to its mix of forest and river-based experiences.

Planning notes

Build Uganda around route logic: Entebbe entry, then Kibale, Queen Elizabeth, Bwindi, and Lake Bunyonyi or Lake Mburo when time allows. Gorilla and chimp permits should be secured before lodge choice, and Bwindi accommodation must match the trekking sector.
